name: Jerbourg Kiosk
note: Cliff top, sea views to Herm/Sark
hours: Not formally confirmed, seasonal daytime hours.
parking: Ample car park at Jerbourg Point, but the kiosk itself gets busy, arrive early.

name: Cobo Tea Room
note: Right on the bay, known for cakes
parking: Limited right outside, larger Cobo Coast Road car park ~100m north.

name: Mocca Coffee House
note: Locals' favourite for coffee quality
hours: Opens 7am daily, breakfast from 7:30am (closing time not confirmed).
parking: Old Quarter, nearest is Le Pollet/town car parks, short walk.

name: Woodies
note: Outdoor kiosk, views to Herm
parking: No dedicated car park, nearest is Victoria (Crown) Pier, ~200m.

name: The Beach Café
note: Right on the beach
parking: No parking at Fermain Bay itself, walk down Fermain Lane or the cliff path.

name: Gusto
note: Pasta. Closed Sundays. Suggested for Sat 5 Sept birthday dinner, to book
booking: Recommended, small restaurant. Call 01481 722828 or email book@gusto.gg
parking: Town centre, disc-zone street parking nearby or Beau Sejour/Market car parks.

name: Rosso Pizza and Bar
address: North Esplanade, St Peter Port, Guernsey
note: Full vegan pizza menu
hours: Lunch and dinner daily (exact times not confirmed, call ahead).
parking: Free parking available on North Esplanade.

name: Crabby Jack's
note: Veggie burgers specifically praised
hours: Mon 12:00-21:00, Tue closed, Wed-Thu 12:00-21:00, Fri-Sat 12:00-21:30 (check Sun).
parking: Own car park at the front of the venue.

name: Baan Thai
address: Mill St, St Peter Port, Guernsey
note: Small, book ahead
booking: Call 01481 725012, online booking also available.

name: Búho
note: Hotel restaurant, not standalone
booking: Book via Dish Cult or the hotel, recommended for peak times.
parking: Free parking at Fermain Valley Hotel.

name: Ship & Crown
note: Confirmed gluten-free menu/fryer
parking: Limited/metered street parking on North Esplanade, check signage.

name: Good Rebel
note: Breakfast/brunch/small plates only

name: The Rockmount
note: Also a pub, gastropub food
hours: Mon-Fri noon-2:30pm & 6-9pm. Sat noon-3pm & 6-9:30pm. Sun noon-3pm & 5:30-8:30pm (summer).
parking: Large free car park round the back, plus more at the water's edge.

name: Houmet Tavern
note: Pub food
parking: No dedicated car park nearby, check for roadside options.

name: Cobo Bay Hotel
note: 2 AA Rosettes
booking: 01481 264181 or book online at cobobayhotel.com.
parking: Hotel car park on Cobo Coast Road.

name: The Beach House
note: Brunch/café
hours: Seasonal, varies. Email ahead to confirm.
parking: Own free car park next to the restaurant.

name: Port Grat
note: Hidden gem, sheltered swimming
parking: Small car parks at either end, opposite Vardes Quarry or by Rousse Tower.

name: Port Soif
note: Secluded, quiet
parking: Free car park by the café kiosk, ample space.

name: Saints Bay
note: Quiet, clean water, calm swimming
parking: Limited roadside parking down to the beach.

name: Petit Bôt
note: Sandy, historic tower on beach
parking: Free parking for ~40 cars by the beach, plus more up the hill (short walk down).

name: Fermain Bay
note: Tucked away, pebbly
parking: Very limited, car park halfway down Fermain Lane (walk the rest), or Becquet Road to the north.

name: Petit Port
note: 270+ steep steps down cliff. Very small, secluded
parking: Small car park nearby, may have a small fee at busy times.

name: Vazon Bay
note: Popular, longest beach on the island
parking: Plenty of free parking along the coast road.

name: Cobo Bay
note: Popular, sheltered
parking: Car parks at both ends of the beach.

name: Shell Beach
note: "Quiet even when busy"
parking: Park at North Beach car park in St Peter Port before the Herm ferry, no cars on Herm itself.

name: Marble Bay
note: Small, steep walk, secluded
parking: Park at Jerbourg and walk down the steep steps to the cliff path.

name: Grandes Rocques / Saline Bay
note: Sheltered, sand dunes
parking: Free car parks off Rue de la Saline, close to the beach.

name: L'Ancresse Bay
note: Large sandy bay
parking: Large free car park at both ends of the bay.

name: Havelet Bay
note: Reliable spot for seal sightings from shore
parking: Parking along the beach front, time-restricted in summer months.

name: The Golden Lion
note: Best ale range (6 handpumps), CAMRA Pub of the Year 2019/2020
parking: Town centre, no dedicated car park, use nearby public car parks.

name: The Red Lion
note: Randalls' (local brewery) home pub
parking: On the edge of town, check street parking nearby.

name: The Cock and Bull
note: Has a pool table (lower level), live music
parking: Old Quarter, use town car parks.

name: Fleur du Jardin
note: Gardens, cosy, outside town
parking: Own free car park, can fill up in summer.

name: Puffin & Oyster
note: Sheltered seating over Grand Havre, dog friendly
hours: Mon-Thu noon-2:30pm & 5:30-8:30pm, Fri noon-2:30pm & 5:30-9pm, Sat 8:30-10:30am/noon-2:30pm/5:30-9pm, Sun 8:30-10:30am/noon-4pm.
parking: Plenty of parking on site.

name: Castle Cornet
note: Guided tour included, ~3 hrs
booking: Guided tour included with entry, no pre-booking required.
parking: On-street disc-zone parking near the harbour (parking clocks needed, £5.50), or town car parks, 10-15 min walk.

name: Hauteville House (Victor Hugo's House)
note: Book ahead, closed Wednesdays
booking: Online booking essential, guided tours only (10 people/tour, 1 hour). 01481 721911.
parking: Old Quarter, use town car parks.

name: The Little Chapel
note: Quick visit, free/donation
parking: Small free car park (~8-10 cars) plus the Martyn Guille public car park 200m away.

name: Guernsey Museum at Candie
note: In Candie Gardens
parking: No parking in the gardens, nearest is Monument Gardens (5 min walk) or Beau Sejour (7 min walk).

name: German Occupation Museum
note: One man's 60-year private collection. Cash only, closes 1pm
booking: Cash only, cards not accepted.
parking: Own grounds, close to the airport.

name: Fort Grey Shipwreck Museum
note: Small, tidal causeway fort
parking: Ample parking at Guernsey Pearl, opposite, across the causeway.

name: Sausmarez Manor / ArtParks
note: House tour + sculpture garden (coords approximate)
hours: Sculpture park daily 10am-5pm year-round (closed around Christmas).
booking: Grounds need no booking, but the Wednesday 6:30pm manor tour must be pre-booked.

name: Art for Guernsey
note: Small gallery, genuinely good exhibitions
booking: Free entry, no booking needed.

name: La Vallette Underground Military Museum
note: Paid entry, actual U-boat fuel tunnels
hours: Seasonal, varies, roughly midday-5pm, check ahead. Call 01481 722300.
booking: Pay on the door, card accepted.

name: German Naval Signals HQ
note: Paid entry, fully restored, "a must see"
booking: Group tours by advance booking, email museums@gov.gg or call 01481 226518.
parking: No dedicated car park, nearest is Candie Gardens area.

name: Batterie Mirus
note: Guided tour only, book via Tours of Guernsey
hours: Guided tour only, roughly monthly, ~2 hrs.
booking: Book via toursofguernsey.com, sells out quickly, free cancellation up to 24hrs ahead.

name: Batterie Scharnhorst
note: Guided tour only, book via Tours of Guernsey
booking: Book via toursofguernsey.com, sells out quickly.

name: Folk & Costume Museum
note: National Trust of Guernsey, free entry
hours: 31 Mar-25 Oct, daily 10am-5pm (last entry 4:15pm). Closed 9 May (Liberation Day).
parking: Saumarez Park car parks, see Saumarez Park entry.

name: Victorian Shop & Parlour
note: National Trust of Guernsey, dog friendly
hours: 16 Mar-3 Oct, Mon-Sat 10am-4pm. Closed Sundays and Bank Holidays.
parking: Old Quarter, use town car parks.

name: Candie Gardens
note: Free public gardens
hours: Dawn to dusk, free entry, year-round.
parking: No parking in the gardens themselves, nearest is Monument Gardens (5 min) or Beau Sejour (7 min).

name: Saumarez Park
note: Duck pond, houses Folk Museum
hours: Dawn to dusk, free entry, year-round.
parking: Two free car parks (Route de Saumarez by the playground, and Saumarez Lane near the pond), plus overflow at Home Farm Field.

name: Victorian Walled Kitchen Garden
note: Volunteer run, small
booking: Entry by donation, no booking needed.
parking: Saumarez Park car parks.

name: Le Friquet Garden Centre
note: Garden centre + cafe
parking: Own car park, including disabled and parent & child bays.

name: Bordeaux loop
note: Round trip, ~2 hrs. Vale Castle, Dehus Dolmen
parking: Roadside/Bordeaux area parking near Woodies.

name: Wild south-east coast (Fermain/Jerbourg loop)
note: Round trip, 3–4 hrs. Wildest, most dramatic, 230+ steps
parking: Start from Jerbourg Point car park, or Fermain Lane (very limited).

name: Petit Port to Saints Bay (the Renoir walk)
note: One-way, ~2 hrs. Follows Renoir's footsteps to Moulin Huet, the Pea Stacks
parking: Small car park near Petit Port, limited roadside parking at Saints Bay end.

name: Island of Lihou
note: Round trip loop, easy, ~2 miles. Tidal causeway, medieval priory ruins, Venus Pool for swimming
hours: Tidal causeway, only crossable at low tide on published opening times (posted at both ends, in the Guernsey Press, and via gov.gg/lihou). Leave the island at least 20 min before the causeway closes.
parking: Three car parks around L'Eree headland.

name: Heart of Guernsey (Saint Andrew's, inland)
note: Round trip, 3 hrs. Little Chapel, historic watermill

name: North-west coast forts (Albecq to Port Soif)
note: One-way, ~2 hrs. Forts, several beaches
parking: Parking at Fort Hommet (Albecq end) and the free car park at Port Soif.

name: Saumarez woodland/nature trails
note: Round trip, ~2 hrs. Gentle, parkland
parking: Saumarez Park car parks.

name: British Red Cross Shop
note: "Always some treasure to be had"

name: Mostly Books
note: Funds Lifeboat/Samaritans

name: Fresh Friday Market
note: Runs every Friday incl. 4 Sept during the trip

name: De La Rue Antiques
note: No review data found, unverified

name: GO Charity (Giving Opportunities)
note: Furniture, house clearance items, "a proper Aladdin's cave". Moved (Jan 2024) to Southside House, South Quay, St Sampson.

name: The Old Quarter
note: Picturesque cobbled-streets area

name: Victoria Tower
address: Victoria Tower, St Peter Port, Guernsey
note: Free, 99 steps, key from Guernsey Museum
hours: Key borrowed from Guernsey Museum during museum hours (last issue 45 min before closing). Closed in high winds.
booking: Free entry, no booking, just borrow the key at Candie Gardens museum.

name: Jerbourg Point
note: Views to France, Sark, Jersey

name: L'Eree Headland
note: Sunset spot, view over Lihou causeway
parking: Three car parks around the headland.

name: Fort Grey / Rocquaine Bay viewpoint
note: Same site as Fort Grey museum

name: La Vallette Bathing Pools
note: Favourite local sunrise spot
parking: On-street marked bays on La Vallette, plus Blue Badge spaces.

name: Fort Hommet
note: 12 structures, includes shell-decorated shrine bunker
parking: Own free car park off Rue d'Albecq.

name: Liberation Monument
note: Sundial marking Liberation

name: Halfway 4.7cm Pak
note: Wn. Schonbucht Mitte Coastal defence gun to prevent enemy landings preserved and under care by Festung Guernsey. See Halfway (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/halfway/4549797577) page for details.

name: M19 Automatic Mortar Bunker
note: One of only 4 bunkers of this type on Guernsey under care by fully excavated in 2010 by Festung Guernsey. See Fort Hommet page for details.

name: Multi-loop holed Armored Turret
note: Stp.Rotenstein  The large armored steel cupola was blown out for scrap post war but the bunker is mostly intact and under the care of Festung Guernsey  See Fort Hommet page for details.

name: Fort Richmond
note: Stp. Reichenberg  A number of small emplacements surround this Victorian Fort. A recent study was carried out by Festung Guernsey with some interesting discoveries.  See Fort Richmond page for details.

name: Multi-loop Holed Armored Turret
note: Wn.Grune-Dune  Built into a anti-tank wall this bunker worked to defend Rocquaine bay from enemy landings. See L'Eree (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/leree-rocquaine/4555213149) page for details.

name: Mirus Batterie Flak Tower
note: 2cm Flak Tower for air defence for Batterie Mirus. Festung Guernsey now looks after this site with the interior in remarkably good condition.

name: Vale Castle
note: Stp.Talfeste  This 15th century Castle was only modified by the Germans in the addition of trenches, machine gun posts and other field defenses.  See Vale Castle (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/vale-castle/4547873471) page for details.

name: Beau Sejour Regiment Command Bunker
note: Two Story Command Bunker for 584th Regiment under the care of Festung Guernsey.  See Headquarters (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/headquarters-5/4547839861) page for details.

name: 4.7cm FestungPak
note: Stp. Langenberg  Anti-tank gun bunker under the care of Festung Guernsey.   See L'Eree (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/leree-rocquaine/4555213149) page for details.

name: Grande Rocque M19 Automatic Mortar Bunker
H02
note: Large concrete lined munitions tunnel capable of housing vechicles it is now secured with original German items stored in it.  See Tunnels (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/tunnels-7/4547839770) page for details.

name: Grantez
note: This site has numerous light field defences now cleared out by Festung Guernsey and open to the public to view. See Grantez (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/grantez/4547616779) Page for details.

name: Delancey Park
note: Batterie Sperber High vantage point for this site was optimised and emplaced with coastal defence guns as a second line of defence.

name: 10.5cm Coastal Defence Casemate
note: Stp. Rotenstein  One of four 10.5 cm Pak Casemates constructed on Fort Hommet, fully restored by The Channel Islands Occupation Museum.  See Fort Hommet or Museums (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/105cm-casemate/4549836603) page for details.

name: MP3
note: Naval Observation Tower Marine Pleistand 3 fully restored by The Channel Islands Occupation Society. See Pleinmont (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/pleinmont/4547454552) or Museums (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/mp3-tower-pleinmont/4549834410) page for details.

name: Chouet Tunnel
note: This known tunnel was originally used to house generators to power the Chouet Headland it was recently excavated by Festung Guernsey it had been closed up since the 1950's.

name: German Occupation Museum
note: The most comprehensive Occupation Museum in the Island with thousands of items from the Occupation.  See Museums (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/occupation-museum/4549816540) page for details.
booking: Cash only, cards not accepted.
parking: Own grounds, close to the airport.

name: German Underground Hospital
note: One of the largest German tunnel complexes on the Island this site is now open to the public and is well worth a visit. See Tunnels (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/tunnels-7/4547839770) or Museums (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/underground-hospital/4549816588) page for Details.

name: Castle Cornet
note: The Islands most well known Castle it is regularly open to the public with the whole castle a Historic Site and numerous museums in the grounds of the castle.  See Castle Cornet (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/castle-cornet/4547613561) or Museums (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/castle-cornet/4549820329) page for details.
booking: Guided tour included with entry, no pre-booking required.
parking: On-street disc-zone parking near the harbour (parking clocks needed, £5.50), or town car parks, 10-15 min walk.

name: Guet
note: Site of field defences and a large modification to the Guet Victorian Watch House. See Guet (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/le-guet/4549797903) page for details.

name: Batterie Dolmann
note: Restored WWI-era gun, trenches. Four gun pits, a fire control tower, ammunition bunkers. Free entry, public car park off Rue de la Trigale.
parking: Public car park off Rue de la Trigale.

name: Mirus Command Bunker
note: This bunker is connected via tunnel to the Mirus Liestand bunker. This bunker is now secured and used as a store.   See Batterie Mirus (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/batterie-mirus/4547478405) page for details.

name: Vale Mill
note: MP5 Observation Tower the Mill's sails were removed and a aditional two floors were added for observation.  See Vale Mill (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/mp5-vale-mill/4549799308) page for details.

name: Prevote Watch Tower M5
note: Camouflaged WWII watchtower on Prevote Headland, free open access.

name: MP4 L'Angle Tower
note: Guernsey most reconisable German Structure this observation tower is unique in design and like nothing else on the Atlantic Wall. See Pleinmont (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/pleinmont/4547454552) Page for Details.

name: MP2 Observation Tower
note: Located at Lihou Headland this tower served the same purpose as the two towers at Pleinmont even though it is built on the foundations of a mill. See L'Eree (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/leree-rocquaine/4555213149) page for details.

name: Batterie Strassburg
note: Artillery Batterie for four 22cm K532(f) guns in open emplacements. See Jerbourg (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/jerbourg/4549834781) page for Details.

name: St Saviours Tunnel
note: This large munitions tunnel was filled with German equipment and secured shortly after the war it was later opened to the public as a museum but was closed again due to problems with land ownership it was recently put up for sale and bought privately. See tunnels page for details

name: Valette Aquarium Tunnel
note: This tunnel was originally built for access to soldiers bay before the war. During the war the Germans enlarged the tunnel and concrete lined it. It is now the Islands main Aquarium.  See Tunnels (http://www.guernseybunkers.moonfruit.com/#/tunnels-7/4547839770) page for details.

name: Tree with German rungs
note: This pine tree even to day still has numerous rungs running up the trunk to a look out position for the Artillery Batterie 'Barbara'.

name: Guernsey Airport
note: GCI

name: The Farmhouse Hotel
note: Where we are staying, 3–8 Sept

name: Visit Guernsey Information Centre
note: Tourist info, worth asking here for a printed Heart of Guernsey walking route map

name: Chateau des Marais (Ivy Castle)
note: Moated medieval castle (pre-12th century), colloquially Ivy Castle, on an ancient mound with Neolithic finds. Free, open access.
hours: Open access, no set hours, outdoor ruin.
parking: Parking off Sir John Leale Avenue, nearby.

name: Guernsey Diamond Museum
note: The only diamond museum in the British Isles, housed in the old John Tann's bankers vault inside Ray & Scott jewellers.
booking: Adults £3, couples £5, children free. Pay on entry.

name: Castle Breakwater and Lighthouse
note: Granite breakwater built against a feared Napoleonic invasion, walk out past Castle Cornet to the 1867 lighthouse. Popular fishing spot.
hours: Open access, but can close for storm damage/maintenance, check Guernsey Harbours before visiting.
parking: Town centre/harbour car parks, short walk.

name: Herm coast path
note: 4 mile circular walk around the whole island on good coastal footpaths, puffin spotting possible at Point Sauzebourge. No routed path shown, island is small and easy to navigate on foot from the harbour.
hours: Open access, plan around ferry times.

name: Isle of Sark Shipping
note: Ferry to Sark, ~55 min crossing. Office at White Rock.
hours: First sailing ~08:00, last ~17:30 (varies by season, check timetable).
booking: Book via sarkshipping.gg. Exchange confirmation for a ticket at the office at least 25 min before sailing.

name: Travel Trident (Herm ferry)
note: Ferry to Herm, ~20 min crossing, roughly hourly in summer. Departs from Inter Island Quay, tickets from the kiosk at the Weighbridge Clock Tower.
hours: Frequency varies by season, check traveltrident.com for current timetable.
booking: Cash preferred at the kiosk; call 01481 721379 for group bookings.

name: Guernsey Coastal Cruises
note: Scenic boat trips on Glad Tidings: a Guernsey coastline cruise (1.5 hrs, past Castle Cornet, the Bathing Pools, Saints Bay) or a Herm & Jethou cruise (dolphins/seals/puffins possible).
hours: Seasonal, check guernseycoastalcruises.com for sailing dates.
booking: Adults £25, seniors £22, children £12, family ticket £65. Book online or pay onboard.

name: Pirate Bay Adventure Golf
note: 12-hole adventure golf course at St Pierre Park.
booking: Adult £7.50, child £4.95, family of 4 £23.
